html:
The Ovimbundu are the largest people of Angola, living on the Bie plateau of the central highlands and speaking Umbundu. The map shows their lands in 1880 and 1900.

They lived in a dozen or so kingdoms, the largest being Mbailundu (Bailundo) and Bie. In the 1800s they were the great caravan traders of west central Africa. Their caravans walked hundreds of miles inland to Lunda and Katanga and brought back slaves, ivory and beeswax, and later wild rubber, to the port of Benguela.

When the rubber boom collapsed around 1900 and Portuguese traders pushed in, the Ovimbundu rose in the Bailundo revolt of 1902. Portugal crushed it and took over the highlands. The Benguela railway, built across their land, carried copper from Katanga. In the late 1900s the Ovimbundu formed the base of the UNITA movement in Angola's civil war.
sum: The Ovimbundu are the largest people of Angola, living on the Bie plateau of the central highlands and speaking Umbundu. The map shows their lands in 1880 and 1900.
